Status

FinKore Core 2.0.3 stable.

Purpose

This document defines validation of financial entity state and proposed domain operations.

Terminology

Structural Validation checks required shape and value forms. Business Validation checks business invariants and State-dependent rules.

Requirements

  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 — A Financial Entity MUST satisfy all Structural Validation and Business Validation rules applicable to its current State.
    Evidence & context2 research notes · 2 practitioner accounts+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Supports the rationale

    Observed input still needs the applicable business validation ↗

    Mohamed Nofel; Mahmoud Marzouk; Hany Elbardan; Reda Saleh; Aly Mogahed

    Declared structural/business validation applies to the complete supplied result, including import. The proposed sensor pipeline motivates that boundary without certifying fact truth, accounting recognition, IoT, blockchain or XBRL.

    Scope and limitations

    This transfer is reviewer inference, not a rule formulated by the authors for FinKore. A sensor’s inventory observation alone does not establish a sale. Cleaning data must not silently invent business facts.

    Research / Supports the rationale

    Changing the representation does not establish equivalent control ↗

    Mysore Ramaswamy; Richard Calvasina; Eugene Calvasina; Gerald Calvasina

    Changing document representation does not itself satisfy the applicable declared financial predicates or eligibility. The historical voucher example motivates control preservation without mandating procurement rules or a document package.

    Scope and limitations

    The transfer to FinKore is reviewer inference. The article’s legal assertions, Just-In-Time process and document package are not verified as current or universal. A syntactically valid message does not itself establish payment eligibility.

    Legacy / Supports the rationale

    Validate supplied financial observations without confusing validity with factual truth ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    All structural and business rules applicable to the current State apply, not an assumed universal application schema.

    Scope and limitations

    Product-specific names, address formats and numeric-field rules must be declared by a composing domain. The anecdote supplies no universal input grammar or guarantee that a validator detects fraud, missing facts, or all bad assumptions. FinKore validates declared conditions against supplied observations; it does not certify their real-world truth.

    Legacy / Supports the rationale

    Keep institution-specific business rules explicit rather than treating one practice as universal ↗

    Otilia Borges

    An Entity must satisfy the Structural and Business Validation rules applicable to its current State. Applicability is required; a universal institution- or country-specific rule set is not supplied.

    Scope and limitations

    The account does not establish the content or legal validity of any current regulation, nor does it turn a bank-specific rule into FinKore Core. The 1990 Collor Plan and printed-report story are not reconstructed as portable account-freeze or regulator-submission operations. CORE-002.2 governs financial-change validation, not a jurisdictional policy catalog. ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 requires applicable rules to hold without selecting the business rules for every bank, product or country.

  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-004 — Failure of a Structural Validation or Business Validation rule defined for the Financial Entity MUST identify FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED. Stable violation identifiers follow ENTITY-ERROR-002, and preservation of a primary domain-specific code follows ENTITY-ERROR-004.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-005 — Validation details SHOULD identify relevant domain paths.
    Evidence & context1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Legacy / Supports the rationale

    Stable portable failures and actionable diagnostics serve different readers ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Relevant domain paths are SHOULD-level guidance; preserve published coverage limitations.

    Scope and limitations

    The quote is advice supported by a personal incident, not a FinKore requirement for log content, manuals, localized wording, or an error envelope. SPEC-ERROR-003 permits messages and context (MAY); entity paths and stable violation identifiers are SHOULD obligations. Sensitive financial, personal and implementation data are not automatically safe to include.

  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-008 — Validation details MUST NOT expose sensitive values unnecessarily.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-006 — Validation evaluation MUST NOT alter the observable Financial Entity.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-007 — A composing domain SHOULD distinguish rules required in every state from rules required only for a transition or target state.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-009 — An unsupported or malformed Entity validator declaration MUST be rejected with FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_MUTATION before evaluating declared predicates against Entity data. It MUST NOT be silently skipped. A supported, well-formed rule that rejects data continues to use FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED under ENTITY-VALIDATION-004. Rejection MUST preserve existing Entity observations.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-010 — The bounded Entity representation MUST supply object-valued data at creation and at every boundary consuming an existing Entity observation, including import and evolution. Omission, null, or non-object data MUST use FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED, even when no business validator is declared. This requirement defines the bounded fixture shape, not a universal composing-domain data schema. Failure MUST preserve prior observations and MUST NOT expose a partial result.
  • ENTITY-VALIDATION-011 — An implementation accepting native Entity application data MUST document its supported value profile, capture independently owned containers, and retain only supported immutable scalar values. Supported values MUST preserve their exact meaning, including all JSON object member names, through construction, observation, import, mutation, transition and evolution. Caller mutation of inputs or returned observations MUST NOT rewrite another retained Entity observation. Mutable or unsupported numeric objects, unsupported numeric subclasses, non-finite values, other unsupported objects and cyclic containers MUST be rejected without coercion, rounding, invoking custom copy hooks or partial effects. Shared acyclic containers MUST remain valid. Unsupported initial, imported or current Entity data MUST use FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED; unsupported proposed mutation values MUST use FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_MUTATION. Existing definition, identity, Workflow, current-data and mutability validation priorities MUST be preserved. A rejected operation MUST leave Entity, revision, evolution and Audit observations unchanged.

Native application-data profile

ENTITY-VALIDATION-011 extends the retained-value discipline of APPROVAL-FACT-004 to Entity application data. The bounded profile consists of null, strings, Booleans, supported finite numbers, arrays/lists and string-key objects/maps. Entity data itself remains object-valued under ENTITY-VALIDATION-010. Containers are copied independently; accepted immutable numbers retain exact values without converting exact decimals through binary floating point. Numeric strings remain strings; Money is not inferred from shape. TypeScript accepts dense indexed arrays and plain or null-prototype records, with string-key own enumerable members; symbol-key records and missing array positions are unsupported. Python accepts lists and string-key dictionaries; Java accepts lists and string-key maps. Container copying does not invoke custom copy hooks.

The reference native numeric sets are finite primitive TypeScript number; exact Python built-in int, finite built-in float and finite Decimal; and exact Java classes Byte, Short, Integer, Long, BigInteger, BigDecimal, finite Float and finite Double. Numeric subclasses, mutable Number objects such as AtomicInteger/AtomicLong, TypeScript bigint/boxed numbers and other native objects are unsupported. This does not add a persistence encoding, extend Workflow guard comparison, or alter Money arithmetic/rounding rules.

The application-data profile applies to source and related/successor Entity data in evolution. Audit evidence has its own value profile; this does not define a total ordering for otherwise unspecified competing errors.

Invariants

A successful operation must leave the Financial Entity valid for its resulting State. A failed operation must leave the Financial Entity unchanged.

For an Entity lifecycle Transition, the complete proposed result includes the target State even when the data is unchanged. Rules declared for that target State are evaluated only after the referenced Workflow accepts the Transition Request and its Guards. A supported target-State rule that rejects the proposed Entity uses ENTITY-VALIDATION-004 and leaves the original observation unchanged under ENTITY-VALIDATION-006. This ordering does not replace an earlier primary Workflow error and does not define the outcome for malformed Entity guard-context containers.

The applicable rules in ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 also govern Entity observations supplied as the source, related Entity, or successor of an evolution operation. Preserving source facts does not waive their declared validation, and an operation cannot successfully identify an invalid related Entity as its domain result. Validate each complete observation against the rules applicable to its State. A declared business-validator failure uses ENTITY-VALIDATION-004; preservation of a more specific primary domain failure still follows ENTITY-ERROR-004. Failed evolution returns no partial relation, currentness change, or Audit commit under ENTITY-EVOLUTION-023 and ENTITY-EVOLUTION-033.

Example

The following JSON is illustrative and non-normative.

{
  "code": "FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED",
  "violations": [
    { "rule": "AMOUNT_REQUIRED", "path": "amount" }
  ]
}

Cross-field example (non-normative)

For example, a composing domain may declare that an amount must not exceed a limit in the same currency. Updating both from 10 EUR to 20 EUR must be validated against the proposed 20 EUR amount and 20 EUR limit, not against an intermediate 20 EUR amount and old 10 EUR limit. A proposed 30 EUR amount and 20 EUR limit must fail without changing either original field. This is an illustration of ENTITY-VALIDATION-003, not a universal Entity constraint or a standardized validation language.

Invalid Examples

  • Applying half of a multi-field mutation before reporting another field invalid.
  • Using localized prose as the only machine-readable violation identity.

Validator declarations

ENTITY-VALIDATION-009 distinguishes declaration failure from a supported predicate rejecting data. The bounded fixture supports only positive-money and money-not-greater-than, with nonempty string id/path and the latter's nonempty otherPath. A fixture rule may also name a nonempty list of distinct declared States in states; omission applies the rule in every State. Null, empty, duplicate, non-string, or undeclared State selectors are malformed declarations under ENTITY-VALIDATION-009. Omitted validation and an empty list remain valid. No general validation DSL or universal positive-Money business rule is introduced, and no total priority over unrelated domain failures is specified.

Open Questions
